title: Marangoni rods under trait-blind turnover (random whole-body removal, removed matter returned at once): division continues at a steady rate to T~1800 on 2 seeds (40-45 dividing rods vs 19 without turnover, generation 8 and 4), the swim-3-lengths minority stays rare (6 of 85) and is redrawn every cycle (parent-offspring slope of D -0.25 [-0.47, -0.02]); the mar=0 floor has none
summary: Loop 2 of Q:marangoni-turnover-persistence. With p 0.10 removal every 10 frames and REDIST (removed matter spread back uniformly), T=2000 on seeds 81 and 82: 50 persistent splits on each seed, 3-9 per 40 frames through frame 320-360, labkit generation 8 and 4, 40-45 dividing tracks; the no-dilution run on seed 82 declines to 1-2 splits per 40 frames (19 dividing tracks, 11 in the first cohort). Rods that swim 3 of their own lengths between birth and division: 5 of 45 (seed 81, cohort shares 0 -> 0.40 on 3-14 rods) and 1 of 40 (seed 82); mar=0 floor 0 of 20. Pooled parent-offspring regression of D (c00's analyze.py) on 41 pairs: slope -0.25 [-0.47, -0.02] against a time-matched null of +0.14, so the trait is regenerated, not inherited. Fast rods grow and divide sooner (speed-cycle Spearman -0.52).

finding.operator: trait-blind whole-body removal with immediate uniform return of the removed matter (serial-transfer turnover)
finding.control: same world without dilution (p 0, seed 82); mar=0 floor (seed 81)
finding.result: persistent splits 50 and 50 (turnover) vs 40, declining (none); dividing tracks 45, 40 vs 19; max generation 8, 4 vs 4; D>=3 rod lengths 5/45, 1/40, floor 0/20; D-on-D slope -0.25 [-0.47,-0.02], n=41
